description: Providing relief to people affected by the war situation in the Middle East
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-04-06 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- In order to minimize the impact caused to the day to day living of the general public and overall economy upon the increase of fuel prices due to the war situation in the Middle East region, approval has been given at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-03-30 to provide relief of up to Rs.20/- per litre of 92 octane petrol and up to Rs.100/- per litre of auto diesel used for public transportation. In addition to the relief provided in general, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to provide relief as follows to low-income earners, electricity consumers, farmers, fishermen and small tea growers who have been directly affected by the increase in energy prices: (i) Providing an additional special allowance for the month of April 2026 to low-income groups registered under the Aswesuma programme, regardless of the number of members in a family:

Providing an amount of Rs.7,500/- to a family in the extreme poor category.


Providing an amount of Rs.5,000/- to a family in the poor category.


Providing an amount of Rs.2,500/- to a transitional family.

(ii) Instead of passing the additional cost incurred for the deployment of thermal power plants to generate electricity due to the increase in fuel prices and the prevailing dry weather condition, to electricity consumers, the Government to bear the relevant additional cost for a period of 03 months so that relief can be provided to electricity consumers of less than 90 units.(iii) Increase the fertilizer subsidy of Rs.25,000/- currently provided per hectare to Rs.30,000/- for the Yala season and increase the fertilizer subsidy of Rs.15,000/- currently provided per hectare for additional crops grown in paddy fields, to Rs.18,000/- for the Yala season.(iv)  Facilitate for the provision of a 50 kg bag of urea fertilizer required for the Yala season to farmers through Agrarian Service Centres at a fixed price of Rs.10,200/- per bag.(v) Provide a subsidy of Rs.50/- per litre of fuel for oneday fishing vessel operating in the fishing industry for a period of 03 months at a rate of 25 litres per day for a maximum of 25 days per month.(vi)     Provide one-time payment of Rs.150,000/- for a multi-day fishing vessel engaged in the fishing industry for the ensuing 03 months.(vii) Provide an additional one-time payment of Rs.5,000/- for a 50 kg bag of fertilizer for small tea growers who are currently receiving a fertilizer subsidy of Rs.4,000/- by the Sri Lanka Tea Board.
